mainEntity.name: What can AI actually do for video creation and editing, and what still needs to be done by a person?

acceptedAnswer.text: AI-assisted video creation can help with research, outlines, scripts, shot lists, captions, rough cuts, audio cleanup, and short-form repurposing. It works best as a supervised workflow, not a one-click replacement for creative judgment. For Run My AI Business readers, the practical starting point is to choose one repeatable video task—such as turning a newsletter or lesson into clips—and define the desired audience, format, length, tone, and approval steps before selecting software. Key factors include source-material quality, brand voice, export needs, accessibility, and whether the tool supports your existing workflow. Create a low-cost draft first, inspect every scene and caption, then revise manually before publishing. Run My AI Business can help readers evaluate video workflows as part of a broader digital-product or content system without presenting AI output as finished work.
acceptedAnswer.description: AI can assist with scripts, storyboards, captions, rough cuts, audio cleanup, resizing, and clip selection. A person should still approve facts, pacing, visuals, permissions, brand voice, and the final export. Start with one repeatable task, test it on a short project, and add review checkpoints before anything is published.
